title: Conditional fifth-moment hard-cutoff corridor for the Q3 projected-D/delta-D route
question: Given the registered two-orientation twentieth-moment envelope, does the declared hard cutoff L=R^(2/5) produce a vanishing polynomial tail and a factorial shell remainder?
method: Recompute m_R=6R(2R+1)^2 and the safe inequality m_R<=54R^3 on exact fifth-power radii R=1,32,3125.
Apply the registered hard-tail formula m_R^2 c^2 M20 L^(-16) with L=R^(2/5), and independently recompute the safe corridor 2916 c^2 M20 R^(-2/5).
Evaluate the scalar factorial shell (C R^(4/5))^R/R! in the log domain and compare it with (e C R^(-1/5))^R.
Compile Lean R283 for exact rational instances of the multiplicity, cutoff, factorial and scope arithmetic; retain the registered M20/history theorem as a cited premise.
finding: Primary 22/22, independent 17/17, integrated 14/14, and Lean R283 compile PASS. The exact fifth-power fixtures give L=1,4,25 for R=1,32,3125. The safe two-orientation tail values are 2916, 729 and 2916/25=116.64, with the exponent reduction 6-(2/5)*16=-2/5. The factorial scalar log comparison gives bases e, 1.3591409142 and 0.5436563657; at R=3125 the exact log is -1909.4360 and the elementary majorant log is -1904.4935.
decision_reason: The package makes the registered fifth-moment-to-hard-cutoff interface explicit and independently reproducible. It closes the scalar multiplicity and exponent bookkeeping that the direct D/delta-D corridor needs, while preserving the distinction between a supplied Q3 M20/history estimate and the missing unbounded common-core theorem.
boundary: This is a conditional scalar hard-cutoff corridor. It converts a supplied M20/history envelope into a vanishing polynomial cutoff tail and a scalar factorial-shell estimate. It does not supply the actual Q3 M20 theorem, a common core, a source/volume-uniform modular history, direct D or delta-D Cauchy convergence, a common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, a gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure.
next_action: Use the corridor only after proving the actual Q3 common-core M20 and modular-domain hypotheses; then establish full-versus-cutoff D/delta-D convergence and exhaustion independence before any common-alpha identification.
no_overclaim: The scalar tail and factorial limits are conditional interfaces, not a thermodynamic dynamics theorem and not an OS/KMS/GNS or Pre-A result.

qft_interface.closed: Conditional scalar hard-cutoff power and factorial-shell bridge under the registered fifth-moment/history premise.
qft_interface.open: Actual Q3 M20 uniformity, common-core/truncated-CCR transfer, direct D/delta-D Cauchy, product/core density, exhaustion independence, group law, common alpha, OS/KMS identification, GNS gap, continuum, C6, Sector A and Pre-A.
qft_interface.tect_boundary: No heat_root_incidence or canonical A1/R-192 production owner is supplied.

adversarial_review.check: M20 is cited as a fixed-beta periodic compact-source premise; this package does not extend it to arbitrary volume, source, beta, orientation or history.
Both lanes recompute m_R and verify the 54 and 2916 safety constants on exact fifth-power radii.
The exact fixtures choose R=1,32,3125 so R^(1/5), R^(2/5), and R^(4/5) are integers; symbolic exponent reduction is kept separate from finite matrix data.
The factorial lane uses R! >= (R/e)^R only as a scalar majorant and never calls it a Dyson or Q3 convergence proof.
No direct D/delta-D, common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector A or Pre-A closure is inferred.
